sources.title: The keeper of the footbridge
sources.text: Pip is a rabbit who lives in a burrow beside the meadow footbridge. Every morning Pip carries a small amber lantern to the bridge.

sources.title: A crossing after sunrise
sources.text: The meadow footbridge opens after sunrise and closes at dusk. Pip waits on the near bank when the bridge is closed. The bridge never opens at night.

sources.title: The view from Clover Hill
sources.text: In the fictional Meadow Atlas, a rainbow appears above Clover Hill when the sun follows rain. The rainbow can be seen from the hill, but not from inside Pip's burrow.

sources.title: The hilltop observatory
sources.text: A brass telescope stands on Clover Hill. Mira the fox tends it. Visitors look at the moon through the telescope after dusk; the telescope cannot see through clouds.

sources.title: What the river carries
sources.text: The river runs beneath the footbridge. A paper boat may drift downstream, but nobody in Meadow Atlas can walk on water. Reeds shelter small silver fish.

sources.title: A place to leave a letter
sources.text: A blue postbox stands beside the meadow garden. Pip leaves letters there for Mira. Sunflowers turn the garden gold in summer, and a stone bench offers a place to read.

sources.title: Light for the path
sources.text: Pip's lantern glows amber. It lights the path, but it cannot change the weather or make the bridge open. At night, white stars appear between the clouds.

sources.title: An earlier crossing rule
sources.text: An earlier Meadow Atlas draft said the footbridge stayed open all night. This draft is replaced by A crossing after sunrise, version 1, and must not govern a new story.
